name: MCP tool call
description: Calls one tool on one MCP server declared in settings.json, and stores what it answered as artifacts. No AI involved - the same servers an ai@1 session gets, reached directly when the work needs no model.

args.name: server
args.label: Server
args.description: The name of a server declared under ai.mcpServers in settings.json. A task chooses among the machine's servers; it cannot declare one.

args.name: tool
args.label: Tool
args.description: The tool's bare name, as the MCP view lists it - wit_get_work_item, not ado-wit_get_work_item. The wire prefix is a session's concern, not this task's.

args.name: arguments
args.label: Arguments
args.description: The tool's own arguments, handed over as written. Nothing here checks them - the shape belongs to the server, so a wrong name fails at the server rather than before the run.

args.name: allowedEnv
args.label: Allowed env vars
args.description: Extra environment variable names this task grants the server declaration, for a ${{ env.NAME }} inside it. env.denied still vetoes.

args.name: timeoutMs
args.label: Timeout (ms)
args.description: Ceiling on the whole conversation - start, handshake, call. Higher than an HTTP call's default because a stdio server is usually an npx download before it is a server.

args.name: failOnToolError
args.label: Fail on a tool error
args.description: true fails the task when the server marks its answer as an error. false stores it and carries on - for when the error is data a later if: reads.
